Separately, the instrument that reports on this category was repaired: tools/ui-invariants.mjs now declares and actually runs S1, S2, S5 and S6 at 390x844 as well as 1440x900 — printed as '[viewports: 1440x900, 390x844]' — closing state.md's open evidence-fix, and that change immediately caught a real R8 violation in the new mobile record layout during round 3. Density fell measurably on the site's densest surface, at both viewports, as a direct cost of this iteration's two fixes. At 1440x900 the readable table region went from the full 854px below the sticky header to a 661.3px scrollport of which 28.7px is the thead, so rows visible per screen fell from ~27 to 20, a 26% loss; 96px of ground sits empty between the scrollport's bottom edge (722.7px) and the footer top (818.7px) at maximum page scroll. At 390x844 the document went from 13,445px to 86,776px — 103 viewport-heights — at 216px per record, so a screen now delivers 3.9 models where it previously delivered ~24 names. Both figures measured on the tree at build 2026-08-31T22:47:15Z. The anchor's own density complaints (I16's unspent shell residue, /wiki leaving 55% of the shell empty) are untouched. Items I23 and I25.

score_hold_justification: Two impact-9 items closed and the overall moves +0.1 — below NF1's 0.2 floor. That arithmetic is correct and it is the honest reading, for three reasons stated in order of weight. First, only one of the two closures is forward progress. I15 was created by this loop in iteration 1; the anchor's 7.0 was scored on a tree carrying it, so removing it restores a position the loop already held before iteration 1 spent a round trip creating it. Scored counterfactually — what iteration 1 would have earned had it not shipped the regression — list-and-table craft was worth about 6.3, not 5.5, and the trajectory reads 6.8 (iter-00) to ~7.1 (iter-01 without its own regression) to 7.1 (iter-02): one round of genuine gain, one round spent on self-repair. Second, the one genuine gain paid for itself in another category. I1 and I15 both bought their result by removing screen area: the 390px record form is 6.5x longer than the table it replaced, and the desktop scrollport is 23% shorter than the page region it replaced. Information density therefore moves -0.5 against list-craft's +1.5 and responsive integrity's +1.0, which is the contract's relocated-defect case applied to geometry rather than to colour — the reader can now reach every field, and can compare far fewer of them at once. Third, nine of the anchor's fifteen items were not worked at all, four of them deferred by scope rather than declined, so the seven categories they govern were held by construction: family coherence, typography, colour discipline, chrome restraint and first-read hierarchy have no named change in this iteration's evidence and were not moved. The two hard-measured categories are unchanged lookups: axe clean in both themes with a lowest sweep ratio of 150/817 = 0.18 keeps accessibility at 7, and 122.9 KB of 150 KB (81.9%) keeps payload at 9. A +0.1 that sits under the noise floor is not a claim of measurable improvement, and it should not be reported as one.

items.problem: The evidence set the judge was handed was captured from a build one revision behind the tree, and nothing in the set or its manifest says so. loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json records captured 2026-08-31T22:40:05Z; every capture's own footer reads 'built 2026-08-31T22:31:33Z' (legible in the last 320px of current/table-catalog--light--390.png), while out/ is built 2026-08-31T22:47:15Z. The difference is not cosmetic: the 390px catalog document measures 81,157px in the evidence and 86,776px on the tree, and the evidence shows a 1px rule between every stacked record — the R8 shape — which the tree no longer has, because it was removed after the capture (see S2's own falsifier note, 'iter-02 round 3'). A judge scoring the surface this iteration worked from the set provided would have filed a regression against a defect that had already been fixed. The change manifest states the set 'was recaptured after the final change, 40/40 identity-verified'; the identity check verifies route path, non-empty title and <main> character count, none of which can detect a stale build.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json and loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--390.png (footer timestamp 22:31:33Z, document 81,157px) against out/catalog.html (built 22:47:15Z) and the same page measured live at 86,776px
items.invariant: Every capture in an evidence set shall carry the build identifier of the tree it was taken from, that identifier shall be recorded in manifest.json, and a set whose identifier differs from the current build shall be refused as evidence rather than filed as usable.
items.governing_rule: null - checked R1 through R12. None governs evidence provenance; this is the rig's own contract, the same class as R5's preserved post-mortem about a check that passed by not looking.
items.prescription: Read the build id already emitted into every page (the footer's built timestamp, or data/launch.json) at capture time, record it in manifest.json, and re-read it after the last capture. Fail the run if it differs from the id in out/ at the moment of writing. The existing identity block in tools/ui-evidence.mjs is the right place: it already proves each capture is the page it claims to be; it must also prove the whole set is the tree it claims to be.

items.problem: fullPage: true misrenders /catalog at 1440, which is the one route this iteration changed. On the tree, #catalog-table-wrap is 661.3px tall (top 416.3, bottom 1077.7) and .site-footer runs 1173.7-1254.8 in a 1255px document. The fullPage capture paints the wrap 350px tall (white panel from y=416 to y=766, ten rows of 396), puts the footer at ~855, and leaves ~320px of blank ground below it — while still reporting the settled 1255px document height, so the image is internally inconsistent with itself. I reproduced this deterministically: viewport-sized screenshots taken at 0, 200, 500, 1000 and 3000ms after networkidle all render the wrap at its correct 661px, and only the fullPage variant collapses it. The cause is that fullPage resizes the viewport to the document height while the wrap's max-height is calc(100vh - var(--header-h) - var(--footer-h)) and --footer-h was measured once against a 900px viewport. Every route whose layout depends on viewport units is exposed the same way. The practical consequence is the sharpest one this loop has recorded: the change manifest's own account of iteration 2 is that 'the orchestrator caught it by looking at a rendered screenshot' — and the screenshot rig cannot render this page.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--1440.png (white panel 416-766, footer at 855, 320px blank to the 1255px page bottom) against getBoundingClientRect on the same build (wrap 416.3-1077.7, footer 1173.7-1254.8) and viewport-mode captures at five settle delays, all showing 661px
items.invariant: For any route whose computed layout depends on viewport units, the evidence set shall include a viewport-sized capture alongside the full-page one; and any full-page capture whose painted content bottom falls short of the document height it reports shall be refused rather than filed.
items.governing_rule: null - checked R1 through R12. R11's iter-02 addendum establishes that /catalog's geometry is now viewport-dependent by design, which is exactly what makes the capture mode invalid for it, but no rule governs the capture mode itself.
items.prescription: Add a viewport-clipped capture for every route x theme x viewport triple, filed alongside the full-page one, and treat the viewport capture as authoritative wherever the two disagree. As a cheap guard against the general case, assert after each full-page shot that the bottom 32px band of the image is not uniform background when the page has content within one viewport-height of its end. Where a route uses a JS-measured token against 100vh, re-run that measurement after any viewport resize the capture performs.

items.target: app/catalog page template (the 33.999rem stacked-record block in app/globals.css)
items.problem: R12 is satisfied and the reader can now reach every field, but the form it arrives in cannot be scanned. Each record occupies 215.9px — a 31.2px name heading, six label/value lines of 24.9px each, and 35.2px of block padding — so the 396-row catalog is an 86,776px document, 103 viewport-heights at 390x844, delivering 3.9 models per screen. The anchor's complaint was that a mobile reader got 396 names and no numbers; the numbers have arrived and the comparison has left with them. A reader looking for a cheap long-context model can now read any one model's price but can hold at most four in view at once, against 24 before. This is the contract's relocation case in geometry: information hidden behind a horizontal container scroll has been re-issued as vertical distance. Two of the six lines earn little: Read holds the identical string '2026-08-31' on all 396 records (the anchor's I8), and In and Out are a price pair a reader reads together.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--390.png and --dark--390.png for the record form; per-record height 215.9px, document 86,776px and cell geometry measured directly on the tree because the capture set is one build stale (I21)
items.invariant: At 390x844 the /catalog listing shall present at least seven complete model records within one viewport height.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R12 - checked and binding: any tightening must keep model name, input price, output price and lifecycle status per record with no page-level horizontal scroll, and must not reintroduce a header (R11). RULES.md R8 also checked: the round-3 fix carries record separation by padding alone and no remedy may re-add a rule between records to compensate for tighter spacing.
items.prescription: Set In and Out on one line as a price pair, and Context and Status on a second, keeping the label/value alignment; drop Read entirely at this width, since the same date is already stated once in the page's 'last checked 2026-08-31' line and repeating it 396 times is the anchor's I8 defect carried into the mobile form. That is three lines plus the name against the current seven. Tighten the line box from 24.9px toward 20px and the block padding from 35.2px toward 20px. Target under 120px per record, which brings the document under 48,000px and puts seven records on a screen. Note for routing: this is presentation doing what it can. The reader's actual problem is 396 undifferentiated records, which is keeper-gated as I14 — a filtered or paginated catalog would make this item small.

items.problem: The sticky site header is 129.3px tall at 390x844 — 15.3% of the viewport, held permanently, on every route — against 45.8px and 5.1% at 1440x900. Measured at scroll position 1200 on /catalog, /wiki and /, all three identical. It stacks a wordmark line, a nav that wraps to two lines ('wiki catalog tools learn tutorials blog' then 'impossible -> routine'), and a full-width search field with the theme toggle. Chrome that scrolls away costs a reader once; chrome that persists costs them on every screen, and one screen in every 6.5 of the 103-screen mobile catalog is now spent on it. This is structurally invisible to the evidence set, which is captured at scroll 0 in every image (JUDGE.md L3), so it is measured rather than read off a screenshot. It is pre-existing rather than introduced this round, but it is newly consequential now that /catalog at 390px is a 103-screen scroll.
items.evidence: getBoundingClientRect on .site-header at scroll 1200, 390x844, on /catalog, /wiki and / (position: sticky, top 0, height 129.3px, 15.3% of viewport) against the same element at 1440x900 (45.8px, 5.1%); not visible in loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/*--390.png, all of which are scroll-0 captures
items.invariant: The sticky site header shall occupy no more than 10% of the viewport height at 390x844 on every route.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R6 - checked and binding: R6 requires changed-feed lines visible above the fold at 390x844, currently 4 of 24, and a shorter header can only raise that count, never lower it. RULES.md R4 also checked and binding: the search box and the theme toggle must remain reachable AND activatable by keyboard, so they may be collapsed behind a control but not removed from the tab order.
items.prescription: Below 34rem, keep only the wordmark, a search affordance and the theme toggle in the persistent band, and move the seven nav links out of it — either into a disclosure that the wordmark row opens, or into a non-sticky row that scrolls away above the sticky band. Either brings the persistent height to roughly one 44px row plus padding, near 60px. Whichever is chosen, the nav links must stay in the document and in the tab order so R4's traversal still reaches them.

items.problem: Unchanged from the anchor, still unresolvable by this loop, and materially larger after this iteration. /catalog presents 396 rows as one continuous surface with four filter controls and no pagination or grouping beyond an A-to-Z sort within provider.
